html:
A Japanese company based in Kyoto, founded in 1889 by the craftsman Fusajiro Yamauchi to make hanafuda, hand painted playing cards. It became one of the world's largest makers of video games.

For decades cards were its business. In the 1950s and 1960s, under his great grandson Hiroshi Yamauchi, it licensed Disney cards and tried taxis, love hotels and instant rice, with little success, then turned to toys. The engineer Gunpei Yokoi's toys led it into electronics.

Its video game run began in the late 1970s:

  • Donkey Kong in 1981, the first game by the designer Shigeru Miyamoto, which introduced Mario.
  • The Famicom, or Nintendo Entertainment System, from 1983, which revived home gaming after the American crash.
  • The Game Boy in 1989, the Wii in 2006 and the Switch in 2017.

With Sony and others, Nintendo made games one of Japan's great cultural exports, alongside anime and manga.
